title: Oliver's road boy, laundry and uniforms
summary: A road-boy paid by the sidemen handled laundry; the band wore tuxedos in places like Fort Worth.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Okay. When Oliver was on the road, did he have a road manager? Did he have someone to help with the uniforms, or did the musicians take care of all that themselves?

Well, we had a road...we called him a road manager, but otherwise a road... We called him road-boy, you know. He wasn't making very much money, but he happened to be traveling around with the band, you know. Each man in the band would give this guy so much money, you know, at the end of the week to make his salary come up worthwhile, you know. I guess he probably was getting around thirty,

thirty-five dollars a week at least. And each sideman gave him money, we gave him a lot of money, you know. He would take care of the laundry; we'd get in town, he'd find out where the laundry and take all the stuff to the laundry. During that time, he'd take it down early in the morning and get it done that night, before they closed, before the laundry closed. Sometimes it was two days laundry, and he had to see that the laundry would take care of all that, all the cleaning and pressing. We didn't have too much time for that because we was moving all the time, you know.
We (?) our uniforms... We used dark suits, sometimes tuxedos. Mostly tuxedos, because we played some of these exclusive places down South. A place like the Arturi(?) Ballroom in Fort Worth, Texas.
What was the name of that ballroom again?
